description: Palace culture; earliest evidence of some deities (Linear B tablets name a 'Po-ti-ni-a,' possibly Athena or a mother-goddess, and a 'Di-wi-je-u,' possibly Zeus).
The Iliad, Odyssey, and the Theogony are composed (orated/written). The Olympian pantheon takes its classical literary shape.
Great sanctuaries flourish: Olympia, Delphi, Dodona. Vase painting depicts the myths. The Homeric Hymns are composed.
The classical pantheon is fixed; the Parthenon is built for Athena (447–432 BCE). Tragedy and comedy flourish at the Dionysia.
Apollo becomes strongly identified with the sun; mystery cults and syncretism (e.g. Sarapis) spread. Later myths (e.g. Ovid's) are composed.
Greek gods are equated with Roman ones (Zeus=Jupiter, etc.). Pausanias writes his survey of Greek sanctuaries (c. 150–180 CE).
